page.intro: Your app as a real phone app for iPhone and Android: see it here, try it on your phone, and build it for the app stores. Publishing updates it on people's phones, with no new store version.

status.updating: Updating your phone app with this version…
status.upToDate: Phone app is up to date.
status.note: Phones that already have your app get the new version the next time they open it. No new store version is needed.

api.publishFirst: Publish your app first. The phone app shows your published app.
api.noCheck: This page hasn't been checked yet.
api.preparing: Your phone app is still being prepared. Please try again in a minute.
api.noPage: There is no such page in your published app.
api.teamId: An Apple Team ID is 10 letters and numbers, like A1B2C3D4E5. You'll find it in your Apple Developer account under Membership.

preview.title: Your phone app
preview.titleHelp: Your app as a real phone app: drawn with the phone's own text, buttons and lists, not a web page inside a frame.
preview.intro: This is how your app looks and works as a phone app. It is made from your published app and updates by itself every time you publish.
preview.publishFirst: Publish your app first. The phone app is made from your published app.
preview.noWebBuild: The phone preview isn't set up on this server yet. Ask whoever runs it to prepare the native preview.
preview.pageHelp: Choose which page of your app to show in the phone.
preview.iphoneHelp: Show your app in an iPhone.
preview.androidHelp: Show your app in an Android phone.
preview.lightHelp: The phone set to light mode.
preview.darkHelp: The phone set to dark mode. Your app keeps its own colours and look, just as it does on a real phone in dark mode.
preview.languageHelp: See your phone app in each of your app's languages.
preview.compareHelp: Show your website next to the phone app, to see they match.
preview.reloadHelp: Start the phone preview again from the beginning.
preview.loadFailed: Couldn't load your phone app's pages. Please try again.
preview.tapHint: You can tap and scroll in the phone, just like on a real one.
preview.checkTitleHelp: Compares each page of the phone app with your website, picture by picture, so you can spot anything that came out differently.
preview.checkIntro: Check a page to see how closely the phone app matches your website.
preview.checkPageHelp: Compare the page shown in the phone with your website. Takes about half a minute.
preview.checkAllHelp: Compare every page, one after another. Takes about half a minute per page.
preview.checkFailed: The check didn't finish. Please try again.
preview.scoreHelp: {score}% of the page matches your website exactly. Small shifts in text or spacing lower this number even when the page looks right.
preview.preparing: Preparing your phone app from your published app. This takes about a minute the first time…
preview.showPageHelp: Show this page in the phone.
preview.islandsHelp: Parts of this page shown as embedded web views (see below).
preview.islandCount: {count, plural, one {# web view} other {# web views}}
preview.sideBySideHelp: See the website and the phone app next to each other, with the differences marked.
preview.sideBySideCaption: Left: your website. Middle: your phone app. Right: the differences, in red. {score}% matches.
preview.sideBySideAlt: The page {page} on the website and in the phone app, side by side, with the differences marked in red.
preview.differsNote: This page looks quite different in the phone app. <link>See them side by side</link> to find what changed.
preview.webViewsTitle: Which parts run as embedded web views, and why
preview.webViewsHelp: Almost all of your app is drawn natively by the phone. A few kinds of content are shown in a small embedded browser instead.
preview.webViewsIntro: Almost everything in your app is drawn natively by the phone. A few things have no native version yet, so they are shown in a small embedded web view inside the app. They still work and look like your website; they just load like a web page:

reason.iframe: Content from other websites, like maps, videos from YouTube or booking widgets.
reason.canvas: Drawings and games that are drawn on the fly.
reason.script: Parts with their own code, like custom calculators or sliders.
reason.css: A few visual effects the phone can't draw natively yet.

preview.webViewsUnknown: Pick a page to see which of its parts, if any, are web views.
preview.webViewsNone: Every page of your app is drawn natively. Nothing runs as a web view.
preview.webViewsNoneHere: This page is drawn natively. Nothing on it runs as a web view.
preview.webViewsHere: {count, plural, one {On this page, # part runs as a web view} other {On this page, # parts run as web views}}: {reasons}.

reasonShort.script: a part with its own code

phone.title: Try it on your phone
phone.titleHelp: Open your phone app on your own iPhone or Android phone in seconds, without building anything or going through a store.
phone.intro: See your app on your own phone right now, using the free Expo Go app.
phone.loadFailed: Couldn't get the code for your phone. Please try again.
phone.qrHelp: Scan this code with your phone to open your app in Expo Go.
phone.qrAlt: A code to scan with your phone to open your app
phone.getting: Getting your phone preview ready. This takes about a minute the first time…
phone.copyHelp: Copy the preview link, for example to send it to your own phone.
phone.step1: Install Expo Go on your phone. It's free.
phone.appStoreHelp: Open Expo Go in Apple's App Store.
phone.googlePlayHelp: Open Expo Go in Google Play.
phone.step2: Scan the code. On an iPhone, use the Camera app; on Android, use the scanner inside Expo Go.
phone.step3: That's it: your app opens. After you publish changes, it shows them the next time you open it.
phone.previewNote: This is a private preview for you. Expo Go shows a small welcome screen the first time and a tools button; your real app won't have them. Your customers get the real app from the stores (see Build for the app stores below).

browser.title: Try it in your browser (Android)
browser.titleHelp: A real Android phone runs on the server and appears right here, so you can use your app with your mouse and keyboard.
browser.intro: Start an Android phone right here in your browser and use your app on it, no phone needed.
browser.startFailed: The Android phone couldn't start. Please try again.
browser.stopHelp: Turn the Android phone off. You can start it again any time.
browser.until: This phone turns off by itself at {time} at the latest.
browser.idleNote: One phone per person. It turns off after 10 minutes without anyone looking at it, and after an hour at most. If all phones are busy, try again in a few minutes.
browser.modeApkHelp: Install your latest test app on the phone, exactly as your customers would get it.
browser.modeExpoHelp: Open your app in Expo Go. No build needed.
browser.startHelp: Start an Android phone on the server and open your app on it.

stores.title: Build for the app stores
stores.titleHelp: Make the files Google Play and Apple's App Store need, so people can install your app from the stores.
stores.intro: When you're happy with your phone app, make the files the stores need. Publishing later updates your app on people's phones without a new store version.
stores.startFailed: The build couldn't start. Please try again.
stores.testTitleHelp: An Android app you install straight on your own phone to try it, without a store.
stores.playTitleHelp: The file you upload to Google Play Console to put your app in the store.
stores.testBlurb: Install it on your own Android phone to try it: open the file on the phone and allow installing apps from your browser.
stores.playBlurb: The file Google Play asks for. Signed with your app's upload key (made for you the first time).
stores.testTime: Usually ready in under a minute. The first build on a server can take a few minutes.
stores.playTime: Usually ready in one or two minutes.
stores.downloadApkHelp: Download the test app (.apk). Open it on an Android phone to install it.
stores.downloadAabHelp: Download the .aab file to upload in Google Play Console.
stores.downloadSignedApkHelp: The same app as an .apk file, for app stores other than Google Play or to share directly.
stores.buildTestHelp: Make a test app you can install on your Android phone.
stores.buildPlayHelp: Make the file to upload to Google Play. Each new one gets the next build number.
stores.failed: The build didn't finish. Please try again.
stores.testNote: Test apps install over the classic test app, so you can switch between them.
stores.playNote: Google Play only accepts each build number once: every build here gets the next one.
stores.historyHelp: Your latest builds, to download again.

ios.titleHelp: Download your app's iPhone project. Apple only allows building iPhone apps with its own tools, so you build it on a Mac or with GitHub.
ios.intro: Apple only lets iPhone apps be built with Xcode, which runs on a Mac. Download your app's iPhone project and build it on a Mac, or let GitHub build it for you and send it to TestFlight. Either way you need an Apple Developer account ({fee} a year).
ios.mac1: Download the project and unzip it.
ios.mac2: Follow the steps in the README to open {file} in Xcode.
ios.mac3: Choose your team under Signing & Capabilities, then Run it on your iPhone or Archive it for the App Store.
ios.gh1: Put the project in a private GitHub repository (a free account works).
ios.gh2: Add your Apple signing details as GitHub secrets, as the README explains.
ios.gh3: Run iOS (TestFlight) under Actions. Your app appears in TestFlight to test, then submit it to the App Store.
ios.readme: Every step is explained in the README inside the download. Your app keeps updating itself when you publish; you only need a new iPhone version when its name, icon or phone features change.
ios.downloadHelp: Download your app's iPhone (Xcode) project as a .zip file. It takes a few seconds to prepare.
ios.failed: The iPhone project couldn't be made. Please try again.
ios.teamIdHelp: Your Apple Developer Team ID, 10 letters and numbers. It lets links to your app open the iPhone app. Find it at developer.apple.com under Membership.
ios.teamIdHint: Optional. Only needed so links to your app open the iPhone app (see Links that open your app).
ios.teamSaveFailed: Couldn't save the Team ID. Please try again.

links.title: Links that open your app
links.titleHelp: When someone who has your app taps a link to it (in an email, a message or a search result), the app opens instead of the browser.
links.intro: When people who installed your app tap a link to your app's address, the app opens instead of the browser.
links.sharedOnly: Your app uses the shared address for now, so links to it open in the browser. Connect your own domain to have links open your phone app.
links.domainsHelp: Go to the Domains tab to use your own web address.
links.androidStateHelp: Whether Android phones open your app for links to this address.
links.iosStateHelp: Whether iPhones open your app for links to this address.
links.fileHelp: The file phones check to make sure the link belongs to your app. It's made for you.
links.sharedToo: Links to the shared address ({host}) keep opening in the browser.
links.noKeys: Build your app once (test app or Google Play) and this is set up for you.
links.playKeyHelp: Google Play signs the app people download with its own key. Paste that key's SHA-256 fingerprint here so links open the app installed from Google Play.
links.playSaveHelp: Save the Google Play app signing key's fingerprint.
links.playKeyHint: In Play Console, open your app, then Test and release > App integrity > App signing, and copy the SHA-256 certificate fingerprint of the app signing key.
links.iosOn: Ready. In Xcode, turn on Associated Domains under Signing & Capabilities and add <mono>{hosts}</mono>.
links.iosOff: Add your Apple Team ID under iPhone and iPad above, then links open your iPhone app too.

classic.title: Classic (website) app
classic.intro: The earlier kind of phone app: your website inside an app frame. Apps you already built this way keep working, and you can still build them here.
classic.summaryHelp: Show the builds of the classic app, which shows your website inside an app frame.

phonePush.title: Notifications on phones
phonePush.on: Your messages also reach people who use your phone app and allowed notifications.
phonePush.off: Phone notifications aren't switched on for this server yet. Your messages still reach people who allowed notifications in their web browser.
phonePush.adminHow: To switch them on, set NK_EXPO_PROJECT_ID (the Expo project your push credentials belong to) in the server's .env file, plus NK_EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN if your Expo account requires access tokens, then restart the server. Android phones also need the Firebase file (google-services.json) in the phone app, and iPhones an Apple push key in your Expo project. Only administrators see this.
phonePush.help: Phone notifications go through Expo's push service. The server's operator sets them up once for every app.
